picks.style: hieratic greek chant, lyre and low drone, resonant male voice, processional, exalted
picks.why: Empedocles proclaiming himself an immortal god walking into Acragas, garlanded and followed by thousands — the most electric verse in the whole Lives.

picks.style: ancient greek paean, aulos and lyre, male chorus in unison, solemn, rising
picks.why: Aristotle's hymn to Virtue: "better than gold, dearer than parents or soft-eyed sleep" — written to be sung, and it still scans as a hymn.

picks.style: gnomic greek song, kithara, plain steady male voice, riddling, measured
picks.why: The riddle of the year — twelve sons, sixty daughters, white and black, immortal yet all dying — closed and memorable on its own.

picks.style: roman tragic chorus, low strings and hand drum, unison voices, stark, declamatory, slow
picks.why: "Or do we wholly die?" — the great annihilation chorus, ending in smoke vanishing from a hot fire. Fully self-contained.

picks.style: latin declamation set to music, cello drone and struck frame drum, grave male voice, weighty, deliberate
picks.why: "Whoever trusts in a throne... let him look on me and on you, Troy" — a complete argument about fortune with the burning city as evidence.

picks.style: ritual lament, bare hand drums and keening female voices, beaten rhythm, raw, insistent
picks.why: The chorus loosening hair and striking bare breasts to a beat — "we weep for Hector" is already a refrain with a rhythm attached.

picks.style: baroque sacred love song, theorbo and viol, warm soprano, tender, flowing
picks.why: The Canticles paraphrase — "While my Beloved's Mine, and I am His" and the night search through the streets. Sensuous and complete.

picks.style: english verse anthem, chamber organ and natural trumpet, full choir, majestic, striding
picks.why: Psalm paraphrase where the mountains shake, the little hills dance and the waters run backward to tell the news.

picks.style: restoration devotional air, harpsichord and violin, bright soprano, ardent, declarative
picks.why: Cupid dismissed as a guttering taper beside the true God of Love — a single sustained turn of thought, no apparatus.

picks.style: 18th century broadside ballad, fife, snare drum and fiddle, strong male voice, marching, elegiac
picks.why: The Death of General Wolfe — giants storming heaven, a council of Jove, and Wolfe carried off in an urn. A real ballad, complete.

picks.style: colonial parlour ballad, fiddle and hammered dulcimer, gentle tenor, lilting, wistful
picks.why: The castle in the air, with its coral and gold, carried off by a storm the dreamer never felt.

picks.style: revolutionary anthem, fife and drums with massed voices, rousing, moderate march
picks.why: "Be thou for ever, for ever, great and free / The land of Love and Liberty" — an actual repeating chorus, and Paine singing the birthday of a world.

picks.style: georgian anapestic air, guitar and flute, light tenor, brisk, breezily bitter
picks.why: "Phoebe, thank thy false heart" — a clean-limbed farewell in swinging anapests, and the freedom it claims is audibly not believed.

picks.style: english tavern catch, fiddle and drone, ragged male voices, bawdy, bouncing
picks.why: The riddle of the bed: neither male nor female, master and wife both, up when it lies down. Funny, closed, and made for a round.

picks.style: persian-inflected art song, oud and hand drum, husky low voice, swaying, fatalistic
picks.why: Rubaiyat quatrains — the phantom caravan, the row of magic shadow-shapes, take the cash and let the credit go.

picks.style: quiet devotional hymn, sustained strings and low organ, single clear voice, spacious, awed
picks.why: "Something far more deeply interfused" set beside "my soul thirsteth for thee, in a dry and weary land" — two thirsts, one mood.

picks.style: ancient dance tune, double aulos, lyre and clapping frame drum, wordless chorus interjections, quick, circling
picks.why: Only candidate, and it is the dancing-floor of Ariadne: garlands, gold daggers, tumblers whirling through the middle of the ring.
